content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Mártyrum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Martyrs, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Christo profúsum sánguinem,
content.english: The martyrs' triumphs let us sing,

content.latin: Et Mártyrum victórias,
content.english: Their blood poured forth for Christ the King,

content.latin: Dignámque cælo láuream
content.english: And while due hymns of praise we pay,

content.latin: Lætis sequámur vócibus.
content.english: Our thankful hearts cast grief away.

content.latin: Terróre victo sǽculi,
content.english: The world its terrors urged in vain;

content.latin: Pœnísque spretis córporis,
content.english: They recked not of the body's pain;

content.latin: Mortis sacræ compéndio
content.english: One step, and holy death made sure

content.latin: Vitam beátam póssident.
content.english: The life that ever shall endure.

content.latin: Tradúntur igni Mártyres,
content.english: To flames the martyr saints are hailed;

content.latin: Et bestiárum déntibus;
content.english: By teeth of savage beasts assailed;

content.latin: Armáta sævit úngulis
content.english: Against them, armed with ruthless brand

content.latin: Tortóris insáni manus.
content.english: And hooks of steel, their torturers stand.

content.latin: Nudáta pendent víscera,
content.english: The mangled frame is tortured sore,

content.latin: Sanguis sacrátus fúnditur;
content.english: The holy life-drops freshly pour;

content.latin: Sed pérmanent immóbiles,
content.english: They stand unmoved amidst the strife,

content.latin: Vitæ perénnis grátia.
content.english: By grace of everlasting life.

content.latin: Te nunc, Redémptor, quǽsumus,
content.english: Redeemer, hear us of thy love,

content.latin: Ut mártyrum consórtio
content.english: That, with the martyr host above,

content.latin: Iungas precántes sérvulos
content.english: Hereafter, of thine endless grace,

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.
content.english: thy servants also may have place.

content.latin: Psalmus 77(1-8) [1]
77:1 Atténdite, pópule meus, legem meam: * inclináte aurem vestram in verba oris mei.
content.english: 77:1 Attend, O my people, to my law: * incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

content.latin: 77:2 Apériam in parábolis os meum: * loquar propositiónes ab inítio.
content.english: 77:2 I will open my mouth in parables: * I will utter propositions from the beginning.

content.latin: 77:3 Quanta audívimus et cognóvimus ea: * et patres nostri narravérunt nobis.
content.english: 77:3 How great things have we heard and known, * and our fathers have told us.

content.latin: 77:4 Non sunt occultáta a fíliis eórum: * in generatióne áltera.
content.english: 77:4 They have not been hidden from their children, * in another generation.

content.latin: 77:4 Narrántes laudes Dómini, et virtútes eius: * et mirabília eius, quæ fecit.
content.english: 77:4 Declaring the praises of the Lord, and his powers, * and his wonders which he hath done.

content.latin: 77:5 Et suscitávit testimónium in Iacob: * et legem pósuit in Israël.
content.english: 77:5 And he set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.

content.latin: 77:5 Quanta mandávit pátribus nostris nota fácere ea fíliis suis: * ut cognóscat generátio áltera.
content.english: 77:5 How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children: * that another generation might know them.

content.latin: 77:6 Fílii qui nascéntur, et exsúrgent, * et narrábunt fíliis suis.
content.english: 77:6 The children that should be born and should rise up, * and declare them to their children.

content.latin: 77:7 Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscántur óperum Dei: * et mandáta eius exquírant.
content.english: 77:7 That they may put their hope in God and may not forget the works of God: * and may seek his commandments.

content.latin: 77:8 Ne fiant sicut patres eórum: * generátio prava et exásperans.
content.english: 77:8 That they may not become like their fathers, * a perverse and exasperating generation.

content.latin: 77:8 Generátio, quæ non diréxit cor suum: * et non est créditus cum Deo spíritus eius.
content.english: 77:8 A generation that set not their heart aright: * and whose spirit was not faithful to God.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. The Lord set up a testimony in Jacob: and made a law in Israel.

content.latin: Ant. Coram pátribus eórum * fecit Deus mirabília.
content.english: Ant. The Lord did wonderful things * in the sight of their fathers.

content.latin: 77:9 Fílii Ephrem intendéntes et mitténtes arcum: * convérsi sunt in die belli.
content.english: 77:9 The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow: * they have turned back in the day of battle.

content.latin: 77:10 Non custodiérunt testaméntum Dei: * et in lege eius noluérunt ambuláre.
content.english: 77:10 They kept not the covenant of God: * and in his law they would not walk.

content.latin: 77:11 Et oblíti sunt benefactórum eius: * et mirabílium eius quæ osténdit eis.
content.english: 77:11 And they forgot his benefits, * and his wonders that he had shewn them.

content.latin: 77:12 Coram pátribus eórum fecit mirabília in terra Ægýpti: * in campo Táneos.
content.english: 77:12 Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, * in the field of Tanis.

content.latin: 77:13 Interrúpit mare, et perdúxit eos: * et státuit aquas quasi in utre.
content.english: 77:13 He divided the sea and brought them through: * and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel.

content.latin: 77:14 Et dedúxit eos in nube diéi: * et tota nocte in illuminatióne ignis.
content.english: 77:14 And he conducted them with a cloud by day: * and all the night with a light of fire.

content.latin: 77:15 Interrúpit petram in erémo: * et adaquávit eos velut in abýsso multa.
content.english: 77:15 He struck the rock in the wilderness: * and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep.

content.latin: 77:16 Et edúxit aquam de petra: * et dedúxit tamquam flúmina aquas.
content.english: 77:16 He brought forth water out of the rock: * and made streams run down as rivers.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. The Lord did wonderful things in the sight of their fathers.

content.latin: Ant. Iánuas cæli apéruit * Dóminus, et pluit illis manna ad manducándum.
content.english: Ant. The Lord opened * the doors of heaven and had rained down manna upon them to eat.

content.latin: 77:17 Et apposuérunt adhuc peccáre ei: * in iram excitavérunt Excélsum in inaquóso.
content.english: 77:17 And they added yet more sin against him: * they provoked the most High to wrath in the place without water.

content.latin: 77:18 Et tentavérunt Deum in córdibus suis, * ut péterent escas animábus suis.
content.english: 77:18 And they tempted God in their hearts, * by asking meat for their desires.

content.latin: 77:19 Et male locúti sunt de Deo: * dixérunt: Numquid póterit Deus paráre mensam in desérto?
content.english: 77:19 And they spoke ill of God: * they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?

content.latin: 77:20 Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ: * et torréntes inundavérunt.
content.english: 77:20 Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, * and the streams overflowed.

content.latin: 77:20 Numquid et panem póterit dare, * aut paráre mensam pópulo suo?
content.english: 77:20 Can he also give bread, * or provide a table for his people?

content.latin: 77:21 Ídeo audívit Dóminus, et dístulit: * et ignis accénsus est in Iacob, et ira ascéndit in Israël.
content.english: 77:21 Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: * and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel.

content.latin: 77:22 Quia non credidérunt in Deo: * nec speravérunt in salutári eius:
content.english: 77:22 Because they believed not in God: * and trusted not in his salvation.

content.latin: 77:23 Et mandávit núbibus désuper: * et iánuas cæli apéruit.
content.english: 77:23 And he had commanded the clouds from above, * and had opened the doors of heaven.

content.latin: 77:24 Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis.
content.english: 77:24 And had rained down manna upon them to eat, * and had given them the bread of heaven.

content.latin: 77:25 Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.
content.english: 77:25 Man ate the bread of angels: * he sent them provisions in abundance.

content.latin: 77:26 Tránstulit Austrum de cælo: * et indúxit in virtúte sua Áfricum.
content.english: 77:26 He removed the south wind from heaven: * and by his power brought in the southwest wind.

content.latin: 77:27 Et pluit super eos sicut púlverem carnes: * et sicut arénam maris volatília pennáta.
content.english: 77:27 And he rained upon them flesh as dust: * and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.

content.latin: 77:28 Et cecidérunt in médio castrórum eórum: * circa tabernácula eórum.
content.english: 77:28 And they fell in the midst of their camp, * round about their pavilions.

content.latin: 77:29 Et manducavérunt, et saturáti sunt nimis, et desidérium eórum áttulit eis: * non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo.
content.english: 77:29 So they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire: * they were not defrauded of that which they craved.

content.latin: 77:30 Adhuc escæ eórum erant in ore ipsórum: * et ira Dei ascéndit super eos.
content.english: 77:30 As yet their meat was in their mouth: * and the wrath of God came upon them.

content.latin: 77:31 Et occídit pingues eórum, * et eléctos Israël impedívit.
content.english: 77:31 And he slew the fat ones amongst them, * and brought down the chosen men of Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. The Lord opened the doors of heaven and had rained down manna upon them to eat.

content.latin: Ant. Deus adiútor * est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.
content.english: Ant. God is their helper, * and the most high God their redeemer.

content.latin: 77:32 In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus eius.
content.english: 77:32 In all these things they sinned still: * and they believed not for his wondrous works.

content.latin: 77:33 Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.
content.english: 77:33 And their days were consumed in vanity, * and their years in haste.

content.latin: 77:34 Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.
content.english: 77:34 When he slew them, then they sought him: * and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.

content.latin: 77:35 Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adiútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.
content.english: 77:35 And they remembered that God was their helper: * and the most high God their redeemer.

content.latin: 77:36 Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.
content.english: 77:36 And they loved him with their mouth: * and with their tongue they lied unto him:

content.latin: 77:37 Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto eius.
content.english: 77:37 But their heart was not right with him: * nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.

content.latin: 77:38 Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.
content.english: 77:38 But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: * and will not destroy them.

content.latin: 77:38 Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:
content.english: 77:38 And many a time did he turn away his anger: * and did not kindle all his wrath.

content.latin: 77:39 Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.
content.english: 77:39 And he remembered that they are flesh: * a wind that goeth and returneth not.

content.latin: 77:40 Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?
content.english: 77:40 How often did they provoke him in the desert: * and move him to wrath in the place without water?

content.latin: 77:41 Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.
content.english: 77:41 And they turned back and tempted God: * and grieved the holy one of Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Deus adiútor est eórum: et Excélsus redémptor eórum est.
content.english: Ant. God is their helper, and the most high God their redeemer.

content.latin: Ant. Redémit eos * Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
content.english: Ant. The Lord redeemed them * from the hand of him that afflicted them.

content.latin: 77:42 Non sunt recordáti manus eius, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.
content.english: 77:42 They remembered not his hand, * in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:

content.latin: 77:43 Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.
content.english: 77:43 How he wrought his signs in Egypt, * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.

content.latin: 77:44 Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.
content.english: 77:44 And he turned their rivers into blood, * and their showers that they might not drink.

content.latin: 77:45 Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.
content.english: 77:45 He sent amongst them diverse sorts of flies, which devoured them: * and frogs which destroyed them.

content.latin: 77:46 Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.
content.english: 77:46 And he gave up their fruits to the blast, * and their labours to the locust.

content.latin: 77:47 Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.
content.english: 77:47 And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, * and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.

content.latin: 77:48 Et trádidit grándini iuménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.
content.english: 77:48 And he gave up their cattle to the hail, * and their stock to the fire.

content.latin: 77:49 Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.
content.english: 77:49 And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: * indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.

content.latin: 77:50 Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et iuménta eórum in morte conclúsit.
content.english: 77:50 He made a way for a path to his anger: * he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.

content.latin: 77:51 Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.
content.english: 77:51 And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: * the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.

content.latin: 77:52 Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.
content.english: 77:52 And he took away his own people as sheep: * and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.

content.latin: 77:53 Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.
content.english: 77:53 And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: * and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

content.latin: 77:54 Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera eius.
content.english: 77:54 And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: * the mountain which his right hand had purchased.

content.latin: 77:54 Et eiécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.
content.english: 77:54 And he cast out the Gentiles before them: * and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.

content.latin: 77:55 Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.
content.english: 77:55 And he made the tribes of Israel * to dwell in their tabernacles.

content.latin: 77:56 Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia eius non custodiérunt.
content.english: 77:56 Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: * and they kept not his testimonies.

content.latin: 77:57 Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.
content.english: 77:57 And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: * even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.

content.latin: 77:58 In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.
content.english: 77:58 They provoked him to anger on their hills: * and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Redémit eos Dóminus de manu tribulántis.
content.english: Ant. The Lord redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them.

content.latin: Ant. Ædificávit * Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
content.english: Ant. God built * his sanctuary in the earth.

content.latin: 77:59 Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.
content.english: 77:59 God heard, and despised them, * and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.

content.latin: 77:60 Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.
content.english: 77:60 And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, * his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.

content.latin: 77:61 Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.
content.english: 77:61 And he delivered their strength into captivity: * and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.

content.latin: 77:62 Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.
content.english: 77:62 And he shut up his people under the sword: * and he despised his inheritance.

content.latin: 77:63 Iúvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.
content.english: 77:63 Fire consumed their young men: * and their maidens were not lamented.

content.latin: 77:64 Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.
content.english: 77:64 Their priests fell by the sword: * and their widows did not mourn.

content.latin: 77:65 Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.
content.english: 77:65 And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, * and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.

content.latin: 77:66 Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.
content.english: 77:66 And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: * he put them to an everlasting reproach.

content.latin: 77:67 Et répulit tabernáculum Ioseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.
content.english: 77:67 And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: * and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:

content.latin: 77:68 Sed elégit tribum Iuda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.
content.english: 77:68 But he chose the tribe of Juda, * mount Sion which he loved.

content.latin: 77:69 Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.
content.english: 77:69 And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land * which he founded for ever.

content.latin: 77:70 Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,
content.english: 77:70 And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: * he brought him from following the ewes great with young,

content.latin: 77:71 Páscere Iacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:
content.english: 77:71 To feed Jacob his servant, * and Israel his inheritance.

content.latin: 77:72 Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.
content.english: 77:72 And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: * and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ædificávit Deus sanctifícium suum in terra.
content.english: Ant. God built his sanctuary in the earth.

content.latin: Ant. Ádiuva nos, * Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris.
content.english: Ant. Help us, O God, our Saviour, * deliver us: and forgive us our sins.

content.latin: Psalmus 78 [7]
content.english: Psalm 78 [7]

content.latin: 78:1 Deus, venérunt gentes in hereditátem tuam, polluérunt templum sanctum tuum: * posuérunt Ierúsalem in pomórum custódiam.
content.english: 78:1 O God, the heathens are come into thy inheritance, they have defiled thy holy temple: * they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit.

content.latin: 78:2 Posuérunt morticína servórum tuórum, escas volatílibus cæli: * carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
content.english: 78:2 They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: * the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth.

content.latin: 78:3 Effudérunt sánguinem eórum tamquam aquam in circúitu Ierúsalem: * et non erat qui sepelíret.
content.english: 78:3 They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem, * and there was none to bury them.

content.latin: 78:4 Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris: * subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt.
content.english: 78:4 We are become a reproach to our neighbours: * a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.

content.latin: 78:5 Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem: * accendétur velut ignis zelus tuus?
content.english: 78:5 How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever: * shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire?

content.latin: 78:6 Effúnde iram tuam in gentes, quæ te non novérunt: * et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocavérunt:
content.english: 78:6 Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee: * and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.

content.latin: 78:7 Quia comedérunt Iacob: * et locum eius desolavérunt.
content.english: 78:7 Because they have devoured Jacob; * and have laid waste his place.

content.latin: 78:8 Ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum, cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ: * quia páuperes facti sumus nimis.
content.english: 78:8 Remember not our former iniquities: let thy mercies speedily prevent us, * for we are become exceeding poor.

content.latin: 78:9 Ádiuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos: * et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum:
content.english: 78:9 Help us, O God, our saviour: and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us: * and forgive us our sins for thy name’s sake:

content.latin: 78:10 Ne forte dicant in géntibus: Ubi est Deus eórum? * et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris.
content.english: 78:10 Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God? * And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes,

content.latin: 78:10 Últio sánguinis servórum tuórum, qui effúsus est: * intróeat in conspéctu tuo gémitus compeditórum.
content.english: 78:10 By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed: * let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee.

content.latin: 78:11 Secúndum magnitúdinem brácchii tui, * pósside fílios mortificatórum.
content.english: 78:11 According to the greatness of thy arm, * take possession of the children of them that have been put to death.

content.latin: 78:12 Et redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum: * impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine.
content.english: 78:12 And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: * the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.

content.latin: 78:13 Nos autem pópulus tuus, et oves páscuæ tuæ, * confitébimur tibi in sǽculum.
content.english: 78:13 But we thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, * will give thanks to thee for ever.

content.latin: 78:13 In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábimus laudem tuam.
content.english: 78:13 We will shew forth thy praise, * unto generation and generation.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ádiuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propítius esto peccátis nostris.
content.english: Ant. Help us, O God, our Saviour, deliver us: and forgive us our sins.

content.latin: Ant. Ego sum Dóminus * Deus tuus Israël, qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti.
content.english: Ant. I am the Lord * God of Israel, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.

content.latin: Psalmus 80 [8]
content.english: Psalm 80 [8]

content.latin: 80:2 Exsultáte Deo, adiutóri nostro: * iubiláte Deo Iacob.
content.english: 80:2 Rejoice to God, our helper: * sing aloud to the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 80:3 Súmite psalmum, et date týmpanum: * psaltérium iucúndum cum cíthara.
content.english: 80:3 Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel: * the pleasant psaltery with the harp.

content.latin: 80:4 Buccináte in Neoménia tuba, * in insígni die solemnitátis vestræ.
content.english: 80:4 Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, * on the noted day of your solemnity.

content.latin: 80:5 Quia præcéptum in Israël est: * et iudícium Deo Iacob.
content.english: 80:5 For it is a commandment in Israel, * and a judgment to the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 80:6 Testimónium in Ioseph pósuit illud, cum exíret de terra Ægýpti: * linguam, quam non nóverat, audívit.
content.english: 80:6 He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph, when he came out of the land of Egypt: * he heard a tongue which he knew not.

content.latin: 80:7 Divértit ab onéribus dorsum eius: * manus eius in cóphino serviérunt.
content.english: 80:7 He removed his back from the burdens: * his hands had served in baskets.

content.latin: 80:8 In tribulatióne invocásti me, et liberávi te: * exaudívi te in abscóndito tempestátis: probávi te apud aquam contradictiónis.
content.english: 80:8 Thou calledst upon me in affliction, and I delivered thee: * I heard thee in the secret place of tempest: I proved thee at the waters of contradiction.

content.latin: 80:9 Audi, pópulus meus, et contestábor te: * Israël, si audíeris me, non erit in te deus recens, neque adorábis deum aliénum.
content.english: 80:9 Hear, O my people, and I will testify to thee: * O Israel, if thou wilt hearken to me; there shall be no new god in thee: neither shalt thou adore a strange god.

content.latin: 80:11 Ego enim sum Dóminus Deus tuus, qui edúxi te de terra Ægýpti: * diláta os tuum, et implébo illud.
content.english: 80:11 For I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: * open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.

content.latin: 80:12 Et non audívit pópulus meus vocem meam: * et Israël non inténdit mihi.
content.english: 80:12 But my people heard not my voice: * and Israel hearkened not to me.

content.latin: 80:13 Et dimísi eos secúndum desidéria cordis eórum: * ibunt in adinventiónibus suis.
content.english: 80:13 So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: * they shall walk in their own inventions.

content.latin: 80:14 Si pópulus meus audísset me: * Israël si in viis meis ambulásset:
content.english: 80:14 If my people had heard me: * if Israel had walked in my ways:

content.latin: 80:15 Pro níhilo fórsitan inimícos eórum humiliássem: * et super tribulántes eos misíssem manum meam.
content.english: 80:15 I should soon have humbled their enemies, * and laid my hand on them that troubled them.

content.latin: 80:16 Inimíci Dómini mentíti sunt ei: * et erit tempus eórum in sǽcula.
content.english: 80:16 The enemies of the Lord have lied to him: * and their time shall be for ever.

content.latin: 80:17 Et cibávit eos ex ádipe fruménti: * et de petra, melle saturávit eos.
content.english: 80:17 And he fed them with the fat of wheat, * and filled them with honey out of the rock.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. I am the Lord God of Israel, who brought you out from the land of Egypt.

content.latin: Ant. Ne táceas Deus * quóniam inimíci tui extulérunt caput.
content.english: Ant. Be not thou silent, O Lord, * for Thy enemies lifted up their head.

content.latin: Psalmus 82 [9]
content.english: Psalm 82 [9]

content.latin: 82:2 Deus, quis símilis erit tibi? * Ne táceas, neque compescáris, Deus.
content.english: 82:2 O God, who shall be like to thee? * Hold not thy peace, neither be O God, thou still,

content.latin: 82:3 Quóniam ecce inimíci tui sonuérunt: * et qui odérunt te extulérunt caput.
content.english: 82:3 For lo, thy enemies have made a noise: * and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.

content.latin: 82:4 Super pópulum tuum malignavérunt consílium: * et cogitavérunt advérsus sanctos tuos.
content.english: 82:4 They have taken a malicious counsel against thy people, * and have consulted against thy saints.

content.latin: 82:5 Dixérunt: Veníte, et disperdámus eos de gente: * et non memorétur nomen Israël ultra.
content.english: 82:5 They have said: Come and let us destroy them, * so that they be not a nation: and let the name of Israel be remembered no more.

content.latin: 82:6 Quóniam cogitavérunt unanímiter: * simul advérsum te testaméntum disposuérunt, tabernácula Idumæórum et Ismahelítæ:
content.english: 82:6 For they have contrived with one consent: * they have made a covenant together against thee; the tabernacles of the Edomites, and the Ismahelites:

content.latin: 82:8 Moab, et Agaréni, Gebal, et Ammon, et Ámalec: * alienígenæ cum habitántibus Tyrum.
content.english: 82:8 Moab, and the Agarens, Gebal, and Ammon and Amalec: * the Philistines, with the inhabitants of Tyre.

content.latin: 82:9 Étenim Assur venit cum illis: * facti sunt in adiutórium fíliis Lot.
content.english: 82:9 Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them: * they are come to the aid of the sons of Lot.

content.latin: 82:10 Fac illis sicut Mádian, et Sísaræ: * sicut Iabin in torrénte Cisson.
content.english: 82:10 Do to them as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara: * as to Jabin at the brook of Cisson.

content.latin: 82:11 Disperiérunt in Endor: * facti sunt ut stercus terræ.
content.english: 82:11 Who perished at Endor: * and became as dung for the earth.

content.latin: 82:12 Pone príncipes eórum sicut Oreb, et Zeb, * et Zébee, et Sálmana:
content.english: 82:12 Make their princes like Oreb, and Zeb, * and Zebee, and Salmana.

content.latin: 82:13 Omnes príncipes eórum: * qui dixérunt: Hereditáte possideámus Sanctuárium Dei.
content.english: 82:13 All their princes, * who have said: Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance.

content.latin: 82:14 Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam: * et sicut stípulam ante fáciem venti.
content.english: 82:14 O my God, make them like a wheel; * and as stubble before the wind.

content.latin: 82:15 Sicut ignis, qui combúrit silvam: * et sicut flamma combúrens montes:
content.english: 82:15 As fire which burneth the wood: * and as a flame burning mountains:

content.latin: 82:16 Ita persequéris illos in tempestáte tua: * et in ira tua turbábis eos.
content.english: 82:16 So shalt thou pursue them with thy tempest: * and shalt trouble them in thy wrath.

content.latin: 82:17 Imple fácies eórum ignomínia: * et quærent nomen tuum, Dómine.
content.english: 82:17 Fill their faces with shame; * and they shall seek thy name, O Lord.

content.latin: 82:18 Erubéscant, et conturbéntur in sǽculum sǽculi: * et confundántur, et péreant.
content.english: 82:18 Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever: * and let them be confounded and perish.

content.latin: 82:19 Et cognóscant quia nomen tibi Dóminus: * tu solus Altíssimus in omni terra.
content.english: 82:19 And let them know that the Lord is thy name: * thou alone art the most High over all the earth.

content.english: Ant. Be not thou silent, O Lord, for Thy enemies lifted up their head.

content.english: ℣. Let them know that the Lord is thy name.

content.latin: ℟. Tu solus Altíssimus super omnem terram.
content.english: ℟. Thou alone art the most High over all the earth.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Ipsíus píetas et misericórdia nos ádiuvet, qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivit et regnat in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. May His loving-kindness and mercy help us, Who liveth and reigneth with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De libro primo Regum
content.english: Lesson from the first book of Samuel

content.latin: 1 Fugit autem David de Naioth, quæ est in Rámatha, veniénsque locútus est coram Iónatha: Quid feci? quæ est iníquitas mea, et quod peccátum meum in patrem tuum, quia quærit ánimam meam?
content.english: 1 But David fled from Najoth, which is in Ramatha, and came and said to Jonathan: What have I done? what is my iniquity, and what is my sin against thy father, that he seeketh my life?

content.latin: 2 Qui dixit ei: Absit, non moriéris; neque enim fáciet pater meus quidquam grande vel parvum nisi prius indicáverit mihi; hunc ergo celávit me pater meus sermónem tantúmmodo? Nequáquam erit istud.
content.english: 2 And he said to him: God forbid, thou shalt not die: for my father will do nothing great or little, without first telling me: hath then my father hid this word only from me? no, this shall not be.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Isti sunt duo viri misericórdiæ, qui assístunt ante Dóminum,
content.english: ℟. These are two men full of mercy, who stand in the presence of the Lord,

content.latin: * Dominatórem univérsæ terræ.
content.english: * The Lord of the whole earth.

content.latin: ℣. Isti sunt duæ olívæ, et duo candelábra lucéntia ante Dóminum.
content.english: ℣. These are two olive trees, and two candlesticks, giving light in the presence of the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Dominatórem univérsæ terræ.
content.english: ℟. The Lord of the whole earth.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Quorum festum cólimus, ipsi intercédant pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. They whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocates with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 3 Et iurávit rursum Davídi. Et ille ait: Scit profécto pater tuus quia invéni grátiam in óculis tuis et dicet: Nésciat hoc Iónathas, ne forte tristétur. Quinímmo vivit Dóminus, et vivit ánima tua, quia uno tantum (ut ita dicam) gradu ego morsque divídimur.
content.english: 3 And he swore again to David. And David said: thy father certainly knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, and he will say: Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved. But truly as the Lord liveth, and thy soul liveth, there is but one step (as I may say) between me and death.

content.latin: 4 Et ait Iónathas ad David: Quodcúmque díxerit mihi ánima tua, fáciam tibi.
content.english: 4 And Jonathan said to David: Whatsoever thy soul shall say to me, I will do for thee.

content.latin: 5 Dixit autem David ad Iónathan: Ecce caléndæ sunt crástino, et ego ex more sedére sóleo iuxta regem ad vescéndum; dimítte ergo me, ut abscóndar in agro usque ad vésperam diéi tértiæ.
content.english: 5 And David said to Jonathan: Behold tomorrow is the new moon, and I according to custom am wont to sit beside the king to eat: let me go then that I may be hid in the field till the evening of the third day.

content.latin: 6 Si respíciens requisíerit me pater tuus, respondébis ei: Rogávit me David ut iret celériter in Béthlehem civitátem suam, quia víctimæ solémnes ibi sunt univérsis contribúlibus suis.
content.english: 6 If thy father look and inquire for me, thou shalt answer him: David asked me that he might run to Bethlehem his own city: because there are solemn sacrifices there for all his tribe.

content.latin: 7 Si díxerit: Bene, pax erit servo tuo; si autem fúerit irátus, scito quia compléta est malítia eius.
content.english: 7 If he shall say, It is well: thy servant shall have peace: but if he be angry, know that his malice is come to its height.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Vidi coniúnctos viros, habéntes spléndidas vestes, et Angelus Dómini locútus est ad me, dicens:
content.english: ℟. I saw men standing together clad in shining raiment; and the Angel of the Lord spake unto me, saying:

content.latin: * Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei.
content.english: * These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

content.latin: ℣. Vidi Angelum Dei fortem, volántem per médium cælum, voce magna clamántem et dicéntem.
content.english: ℣. And I beheld a mighty Angel of God, flying through the midst of heaven, crying with a loud voice, and saying:

content.latin: ℟. Isti sunt viri sancti facti amíci Dei.
content.english: ℟. These men are holy, for they are the friends of God.

content.latin: Ioánnes et Paulus, fratres Románi, cum facultátes a Constántia, Constantíni fília, cui pie fidelitérque servíerant, sibi relíctas in Christi páuperes distribúerent, a Iuliáno Apóstata in númerum familiárium suórum invitáti, líbere negavérunt se apud eum esse velle, qui a Iesu Christo defecísset. Quare præfinítum est eis spátium decem diérum, ut Ióvi sacrificáre induceréntur; quod scelus patráre cum constantíssime recusássent. Terentiáno iúdice, abscíssis domi capítibus martýrii palmam meruérunt. Eórum gloriósus éxitus, a spirítibus immúndis est pervulgátus, qui multórum vexábant córpora; in quibus Terentiáni fílius, et ipse oppréssus a dǽmone, ad sepúlcrum Mártyrum liberátus est. Quo miráculo et is in Christum crédidit, et eius pater Terentiánus; a quo étiam horum beatórum Mártyrum vita scripta esse dícitur.
content.english: The Roman brothers John and Paul distributed to the poor the wealth they had been left by Constantia, the daughter of Constantine, whom they had served justly and faithfully. Invited by Julian the Apostate to join the members of his household, they boldly declared that they did not wish to live in the house of a man who had abandoned Jesus Christ. They were therefore given ten days in which to be persuaded to sacrifice to Jupiter. As they steadfastly refused to commit this sin, they were beheaded in their home, at the command of Terentian the judge, thus meriting the palm of martyrdom. The news of their glorious death was spread abroad by unclean spirits, who began tormenting the bodies of many persons, among them the son of Terentian. He was freed of his diabolical tormentor at the tomb of the Martyrs. This miracle led both him and his father, Terentian, to believe in Christ; and the latter is said to have written the life of the holy Martyrs.

content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

content.english: Ant. John and Paul said unto Gallican: Make thy vow unto the God of heaven, and thou shalt be yet a greater conqueror than ever thou hast been heretofore.

content.english: But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them. In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die, but they are in peace.

content.latin: Perdúcis ad cæléstia:

content.latin: Aurem benígnam prótinus
content.english: Thine ear in mercy, Saviour, lend,

content.latin: Inténde nostris vócibus:
content.english: While unto thee our prayers ascend;

content.latin: Trophǽa sacra pángimus:
content.english: And as we count their triumphs won,

content.latin: Ignósce quod delíquimus.
content.english: Forgive the sins that we have done.

content.latin: Tu vincis inter Mártyres
content.english: Martyrs in thee their triumphs gain,

content.latin: Parcísque Confessóribus:
content.english: From thee confessors grace obtain;

content.latin: Tu vince nostra crímina,
content.english: O'ercome in us the lust of sin,

content.latin: Largítor indulgéntiæ.
content.english: That we thy pardoning love may win.

content.english: ℟. They shall be joyful in their beds.

content.latin: Ant. Isti sunt Sancti, * qui pro Christi amóre minas hóminum contempsérunt: sancti Mártyres in regno cælórum exsúltant cum Angelis. O quam pretiósa est mors Sanctórum, qui assídue assístunt ante Dóminum, et ab ínvicem non sunt separáti!
content.english: Ant. These are the holy ones * who for the love of Christ, recked nothing of the threats of men. In the kingdom of heaven the holy martyrs are filled with joy in the company of Angels. O how precious in the sight of the Lord was the death of these His saints who now stand day and night in His presence and are not divided the one from the other.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos gemináta lætítia hodiérnæ festivitátis excípiat, quæ de beatórum Ioánnis et Pauli glorificatióne procédit; quos éadem fides et pássio vere fecit esse germános.
content.english: Almighty God, fill us, we beseech thee, with the twofold gladness which doth flow down upon this bright day from the glory of thy blessed servants John and Paul, whom one faith and one suffering made to be brothers indeed.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ne discédas a me, * Dómine: quóniam tribulátio próxima est: quóniam non est qui ádiuvet.
content.english: Ant. Depart not from me, * O Lord, for tribulation is very near; for there is none to help me.

content.latin: 21:2 Deus, Deus meus, réspice in me: quare me dereliquísti? * longe a salúte mea verba delictórum meórum.
content.english: 21:2 O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? * Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.

content.latin: 21:3 Deus meus, clamábo per diem, et non exáudies: * et nocte, et non ad insipiéntiam mihi.
content.english: 21:3 O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: * and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.

content.latin: 21:4 Tu autem in sancto hábitas, * laus Israël.
content.english: 21:4 But thou dwellest in the holy place, * the praise of Israel.

content.latin: 21:5 In te speravérunt patres nostri: * speravérunt, et liberásti eos.
content.english: 21:5 In thee have our fathers hoped: * they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.

content.latin: 21:6 Ad te clamavérunt, et salvi facti sunt: * in te speravérunt, et non sunt confúsi.
content.english: 21:6 They cried to thee, and they were saved: * they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.

content.latin: 21:7 Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: * oppróbrium hóminum, et abiéctio plebis.
content.english: 21:7 But I am a worm, and no man: * the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.

content.latin: 21:8 Omnes vidéntes me, derisérunt me: * locúti sunt lábiis, et movérunt caput.
content.english: 21:8 All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: * they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.

content.latin: 21:9 Sperávit in Dómino, erípiat eum: * salvum fáciat eum, quóniam vult eum.
content.english: 21:9 He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: * let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.

content.latin: 21:10 Quóniam tu es, qui extraxísti me de ventre: * spes mea ab ubéribus matris meæ. In te proiéctus sum ex útero:
content.english: 21:10 For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: * my hope from the breasts of my mother. I was cast upon thee from the womb.

content.latin: 21:11 De ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu, * ne discésseris a me:
content.english: 21:11 From my mother’s womb thou art my God, * depart not from me.

content.latin: 21:12 Quóniam tribulátio próxima est: * quóniam non est qui ádiuvet.
content.english: 21:12 For tribulation is very near: * for there is none to help me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 21:13 Circumdedérunt me vítuli multi: * tauri pingues obsedérunt me.
content.english: 21:13 Many calves have surrounded me: * fat bulls have besieged me.

content.latin: 21:14 Aperuérunt super me os suum, * sicut leo rápiens et rúgiens.
content.english: 21:14 They have opened their mouths against me, * as a lion ravening and roaring.

content.latin: 21:15 Sicut aqua effúsus sum: * et dispérsa sunt ómnia ossa mea.
content.english: 21:15 I am poured out like water; * and all my bones are scattered.

content.latin: 21:15 Factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquéscens * in médio ventris mei.
content.english: 21:15 My heart is become like wax melting * in the midst of my bowels.

content.latin: 21:16 Áruit tamquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis: * et in púlverem mortis deduxísti me.
content.english: 21:16 My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws: * and thou hast brought me down into the dust of death.

content.latin: 21:17 Quóniam circumdedérunt me canes multi: * concílium malignántium obsédit me.
content.english: 21:17 For many dogs have encompassed me: * the council of the malignant hath besieged me.

content.latin: 21:17 Fodérunt manus meas et pedes meos: * dinumeravérunt ómnia ossa mea.
content.english: 21:17 They have dug my hands and feet. * They have numbered all my bones.

content.latin: 21:18 Ipsi vero consideravérunt et inspexérunt me: * divisérunt sibi vestiménta mea, et super vestem meam misérunt sortem.
content.english: 21:18 And they have looked and stared upon me. * They parted my garments amongst them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.

content.latin: 21:20 Tu autem, Dómine, ne elongáveris auxílium tuum a me: * ad defensiónem meam cónspice.
content.english: 21:20 But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; * look towards my defence.

content.latin: 21:21 Érue a frámea, Deus, ánimam meam: * et de manu canis únicam meam:
content.english: 21:21 Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: * my only one from the hand of the dog.

content.latin: 21:22 Salva me ex ore leónis: * et a córnibus unicórnium humilitátem meam.
content.english: 21:22 Save me from the lion’s mouth; * and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.

content.latin: 21:23 Narrábo nomen tuum frátribus meis: * in médio ecclésiæ laudábo te.
content.english: 21:23 I will declare thy name to my brethren: * in the midst of the church will I praise thee.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 21:24 Qui timétis Dóminum, laudáte eum: * univérsum semen Iacob, glorificáte eum.
content.english: 21:24 Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: * all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.

content.latin: 21:25 Tímeat eum omne semen Israël: * quóniam non sprevit, neque despéxit deprecatiónem páuperis:
content.english: 21:25 Let all the seed of Israel fear him: * because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man.

content.latin: 21:25 Nec avértit fáciem suam a me: * et cum clamárem ad eum, exaudívit me.
content.english: 21:25 Neither hath he turned away his face from me: * and when I cried to him he heard me.

content.latin: 21:26 Apud te laus mea in ecclésia magna: * vota mea reddam in conspéctu timéntium eum.
content.english: 21:26 With thee is my praise in a great church: * I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.

content.latin: 21:27 Edent páuperes, et saturabúntur: et laudábunt Dóminum qui requírunt eum: * vivent corda eórum in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 21:27 The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: * their hearts shall live for ever and ever.

content.latin: 21:28 Reminiscéntur et converténtur ad Dóminum * univérsi fines terræ:
content.english: 21:28 All the ends of the earth * shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord:

content.latin: 21:28 Et adorábunt in conspéctu eius * univérsæ famíliæ géntium.
content.english: 21:28 And all the kindreds of the Gentiles * shall adore in his sight.

content.latin: 21:29 Quóniam Dómini est regnum: * et ipse dominábitur géntium.
content.english: 21:29 For the kingdom is the Lord’s; * and he shall have dominion over the nations.

content.latin: 21:30 Manducavérunt et adoravérunt omnes pingues terræ: * in conspéctu eius cadent omnes qui descéndunt in terram.
content.english: 21:30 All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: * all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.

content.latin: 21:31 Et ánima mea illi vivet: * et semen meum sérviet ipsi.
content.english: 21:31 And to him my soul shall live: * and my seed shall serve him.

content.latin: 21:32 Annuntiábitur Dómino generátio ventúra: * et annuntiábunt cæli iustítiam eius pópulo qui nascétur, quem fecit Dóminus.
content.english: 21:32 There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: * and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Depart not from me, O Lord, for tribulation is very near; for there is none to help me.

content.latin: Regi sæculórum immortáli et invisíbili, soli Deo honor et glória in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: Now to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

content.latin: In Galátia sancti Crescéntis, qui fuit beáti Pauli Apóstoli discípulus. Hic, in Gállias tránsitum fáciens, verbo prædicatiónis multos ad fidem Christi convértit; regréssus vero ad gentem cui speciáliter datus erat Epíscopus, demum, sub Traiáno, cum Gálatas ipsos usque ad finem vitæ suæ in ópere Dómini confirmásset, martýrium consummávit.
content.english: In Galatia, holy Crescens, the disciple of the blessed Apostle Paul. He made a journey into Gaul, where by the word of his preaching he brought many to believe in Christ. Then he returned home, where he was specially appointed Bishop till the end of his life. He strengthened the Galatians in the work of the Lord, and at last finished his testimony under Trajan.

content.latin: Cæsaréæ, in Palæstína, sancti Anécti Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Urbáno Prǽside, cum álios ad martýrium hortátus esset et idóla oratióne sua prostrásset, a decem milítibus verberári iussus est; ac tandem, mánibus pedibúsque præcísis, truncátus cápite, martýrii corónam accépit.
content.english: At Caesarea, in Palestine, the holy martyr Anectus. In the persecution under Diocletian he exhorted others to martyrdom, and by his prayers caused the idols to fall down wherefore the President Urban caused him to be beaten by ten soldiers, and his hands and feet, and lastly his head, cut off, and so he received the crown of martyrdom.

83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua, Dómine virtútum: * concupíscit, et déficit ánima mea in átria Dómini.
content.english: 83:2 How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts! * my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord.

content.latin: 83:3 Cor meum, et caro mea * exsultavérunt in Deum vivum.
content.english: 83:3 My heart and my flesh * have rejoiced in the living God.

content.latin: 83:4 Étenim passer invénit sibi domum: * et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos.
content.english: 83:4 For the sparrow hath found herself a house, * and the turtledove a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones:

content.latin: 83:4 Altária tua, Dómine virtútum: * Rex meus, et Deus meus.
content.english: 83:4 Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, * my king and my God.

content.latin: 83:5 Beáti, qui hábitant in domo tua, Dómine: * in sǽcula sæculórum laudábunt te.
content.english: 83:5 Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: * they shall praise thee for ever and ever.

content.latin: 83:6 Beátus vir, cuius est auxílium abs te: * ascensiónes in corde suo dispósuit, in valle lacrimárum in loco, quem pósuit.
content.english: 83:6 Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: * in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.

content.latin: 83:8 Étenim benedictiónem dabit legislátor, ibunt de virtúte in virtútem: * vidébitur Deus deórum in Sion.
content.english: 83:8 For the lawgiver shall give a blessing, they shall go from virtue to virtue: * the God of gods shall be seen in Sion.

content.latin: 83:9 Dómine, Deus virtútum, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe, Deus Iacob.
content.english: 83:9 O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: * give ear, O God of Jacob.

content.latin: 83:10 Protéctor noster, áspice, Deus: * et réspice in fáciem Christi tui:
content.english: 83:10 Behold, O God our protector: * and look on the face of thy Christ.

content.latin: 83:11 Quia mélior est dies una in átriis tuis, * super míllia.
content.english: 83:11 For better is one day in thy courts * above thousands.

content.latin: 83:11 Elégi abiéctus esse in domo Dei mei: * magis quam habitáre in tabernáculis peccatórum.
content.english: 83:11 I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, * rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.

content.latin: 83:12 Quia misericórdiam, et veritátem díligit Deus: * grátiam et glóriam dabit Dóminus.
content.english: 83:12 For God loveth mercy and truth: * the Lord will give grace and glory.

content.latin: 83:13 Non privábit bonis eos, qui ámbulant in innocéntia: * Dómine virtútum, beátus homo, qui sperat in te.
content.english: 83:13 He will not deprive of good things them that walk in innocence: * O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.

content.latin: 86:1 Fundaménta eius in móntibus sanctis: * díligit Dóminus portas Sion super ómnia tabernácula Iacob.
content.english: 86:1 The foundations thereof are in the holy mountains: * The Lord loveth the gates of Sion above all the tabernacles of Jacob.

content.latin: 86:3 Gloriósa dicta sunt de te, * cívitas Dei.
content.english: 86:3 Glorious things are said of thee, * O city of God.

content.latin: 86:4 Memor ero Rahab, et Babylónis * sciéntium me.
content.english: 86:4 I will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon * knowing me.

content.latin: 86:4 Ecce, alienígenæ, et Tyrus, et pópulus Æthíopum, * hi fuérunt illic.
content.english: 86:4 Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians, * these were there.

content.latin: 86:5 Numquid Sion dicet: Homo, et homo natus est in ea: * et ipse fundávit eam Altíssimus?
content.english: 86:5 Shall not Sion say: This man and that man is born in her? * and the Highest himself hath founded her.

content.latin: 86:6 Dóminus narrábit in scriptúris populórum, et príncipum: * horum, qui fuérunt in ea.
content.english: 86:6 The Lord shall tell in his writings of peoples and of princes, * of them that have been in her.

content.latin: 86:7 Sicut lætántium ómnium * habitátio est in te.
content.english: 86:7 The dwelling in thee * is as it were of all rejoicing.

content.latin: Ant. Misericórdia et véritas * præcédent fáciem tuam, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Mercy and truth * shall go before thy face, O Lord.

content.latin: 88:2 Misericórdias Dómini * in ætérnum cantábo.
content.english: 88:2 The mercies of the Lord * I will sing for ever.

content.latin: 88:2 In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábo veritátem tuam in ore meo.
content.english: 88:2 I will shew forth thy truth with my mouth * to generation and generation.

content.latin: 88:3 Quóniam dixísti: In ætérnum misericórdia ædificábitur in cælis: * præparábitur véritas tua in eis.
content.english: 88:3 For thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever in the heavens: * thy truth shall be prepared in them.

content.latin: 88:4 Dispósui testaméntum eléctis meis, iurávi David, servo meo: * Usque in ætérnum præparábo semen tuum.
content.english: 88:4 I have made a covenant with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant: * Thy seed will I settle for ever.

content.latin: 88:5 Et ædificábo in generatiónem et generatiónem * sedem tuam.
content.english: 88:5 And I will build up thy throne * unto generation and generation.

content.latin: 88:6 Confitebúntur cæli mirabília tua, Dómine: * étenim veritátem tuam in ecclésia sanctórum.
content.english: 88:6 The heavens shall confess thy wonders, O Lord: * and thy truth in the church of the saints.

content.latin: 88:7 Quóniam quis in núbibus æquábitur Dómino: * símilis erit Deo in fíliis Dei?
content.english: 88:7 For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord: * or who among the sons of God shall be like to God?

content.latin: 88:8 Deus, qui glorificátur in consílio sanctórum: * magnus et terríbilis super omnes qui in circúitu eius sunt.
content.english: 88:8 God, who is glorified in the assembly of the saints: * great and terrible above all them that are about him.

content.latin: 88:9 Dómine, Deus virtútum, quis símilis tibi? * potens es, Dómine, et véritas tua in circúitu tuo.
content.english: 88:9 O Lord God of hosts, who is like to thee? * thou art mighty, O Lord, and thy truth is round about thee.

content.latin: 88:10 Tu domináris potestáti maris: * motum autem flúctuum eius tu mítigas.
content.english: 88:10 Thou rulest the power of the sea: * and appeasest the motion of the waves thereof.

content.latin: 88:11 Tu humiliásti sicut vulnerátum, supérbum: * in brácchio virtútis tuæ dispersísti inimícos tuos.
content.english: 88:11 Thou hast humbled the proud one, as one that is slain: * with the arm of thy strength thou hast scattered thy enemies.

content.latin: 88:12 Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra, orbem terræ et plenitúdinem eius tu fundásti: * aquilónem, et mare tu creásti.
content.english: 88:12 Thine are the heavens, and thine is the earth: the world and the fulness thereof thou hast founded: * the north and the sea thou hast created.

content.latin: 88:13 Thabor et Hermon in nómine tuo exsultábunt: * tuum brácchium cum poténtia.
content.english: 88:13 Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name: * thy arm is with might.

content.latin: 88:14 Firmétur manus tua, et exaltétur déxtera tua: * iustítia et iudícium præparátio sedis tuæ.
content.english: 88:14 Let thy hand be strengthened, and thy right hand exalted: * justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne.

content.latin: 88:15 Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam: * beátus pópulus, qui scit iubilatiónem.
content.english: 88:15 Mercy and truth shall go before thy face: * blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation.

content.latin: 88:16 Dómine, in lúmine vultus tui ambulábunt, et in nómine tuo exsultábunt tota die: * et in iustítia tua exaltabúntur.
content.english: 88:16 They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance: and in thy name they shall rejoice all the day, * and in thy justice they shall be exalted.

content.latin: 88:18 Quóniam glória virtútis eórum tu es: * et in beneplácito tuo exaltábitur cornu nostrum.
content.english: 88:18 For thou art the glory of their strength: * and in thy good pleasure shall our horn be exalted.

content.latin: 88:19 Quia Dómini est assúmptio nostra, * et Sancti Israël, regis nostri.
content.english: 88:19 For our protection is of the Lord, * and of our king the holy one of Israel.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 88:20 Tunc locútus es in visióne sanctis tuis, et dixísti: * Pósui adiutórium in poténte: et exaltávi eléctum de plebe mea.
content.english: 88:20 Then thou spokest in a vision to thy saints, and saidst: * I have laid help upon one that is mighty, and have exalted one chosen out of my people.

content.latin: 88:21 Invéni David, servum meum: * óleo sancto meo unxi eum.
content.english: 88:21 I have found David my servant: * with my holy oil I have anointed him.

content.latin: 88:22 Manus enim mea auxiliábitur ei: * et brácchium meum confortábit eum.
content.english: 88:22 For my hand shall help him: * and my arm shall strengthen him.

content.latin: 88:23 Nihil profíciet inimícus in eo, * et fílius iniquitátis non appónet nocére ei.
content.english: 88:23 The enemy shall have no advantage over him: * nor the son of iniquity have power to hurt him.

content.latin: 88:24 Et concídam a fácie ipsíus inimícos eius: * et odiéntes eum in fugam convértam.
content.english: 88:24 And I will cut down his enemies before his face; * and them that hate him I will put to flight.

content.latin: 88:25 Et véritas mea, et misericórdia mea cum ipso: * et in nómine meo exaltábitur cornu eius.
content.english: 88:25 And my truth and my mercy shall be with him: * and in my name shall his horn be exalted.

content.latin: 88:26 Et ponam in mari manum eius: * et in flumínibus déxteram eius.
content.english: 88:26 And I will set his hand in the sea; * and his right hand in the rivers.

content.latin: 88:27 Ipse invocábit me: Pater meus es tu: * Deus meus, et suscéptor salútis meæ.
content.english: 88:27 He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father: * my God, and the support of my salvation.

content.latin: 88:28 Et ego primogénitum ponam illum * excélsum præ régibus terræ.
content.english: 88:28 And I will make him my firstborn, * high above the kings of the earth.

content.latin: 88:29 In ætérnum servábo illi misericórdiam meam: * et testaméntum meum fidéle ipsi.
content.english: 88:29 I will keep my mercy for him for ever: * and my covenant faithful to him.

content.latin: 88:30 Et ponam in sǽculum sǽculi semen eius: * et thronum eius sicut dies cæli.
content.english: 88:30 And I will make his seed to endure for evermore: * and his throne as the days of heaven.

content.latin: 88:31 Si autem derelíquerint fílii eius legem meam: * et in iudíciis meis non ambuláverint:
content.english: 88:31 And if his children forsake my law, * and walk not in my judgments:

content.latin: 88:32 Si iustítias meas profanáverint: * et mandáta mea non custodíerint:
content.english: 88:32 If they profane my justices: * and keep not my commandments:

content.latin: 88:33 Visitábo in virga iniquitátes eórum: * et in verbéribus peccáta eórum.
content.english: 88:33 I will visit their iniquities with a rod: *and their sins with stripes.

content.latin: 88:34 Misericórdiam autem meam non dispérgam ab eo: * neque nocébo in veritáte mea:
content.english: 88:34 But my mercy I will not take away from him: * nor will I suffer my truth to fail.

content.latin: 88:35 Neque profanábo testaméntum meum: * et quæ procédunt de lábiis meis, non fáciam írrita.
content.english: 88:35 Neither will I profane my covenant: * and the words that proceed from my mouth I will not make void.

content.latin: 88:36 Semel iurávi in sancto meo: Si David méntiar: * semen eius in ætérnum manébit.
content.english: 88:36 Once have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie unto David: * his seed shall endure for ever.

content.latin: 88:37 Et thronus eius sicut sol in conspéctu meo, * et sicut luna perfécta in ætérnum: et testis in cælo fidélis.
content.english: 88:37 And his throne as the sun before me: * and as the moon perfect for ever, and a faithful witness in heaven.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 88:39 Tu vero repulísti et despexísti: * distulísti Christum tuum.
content.english: 88:39 But thou hast rejected and despised: * thou hast been angry with thy anointed.

content.latin: 88:40 Evertísti testaméntum servi tui: * profanásti in terra Sanctuárium eius.
content.english: 88:40 Thou hast overthrown the covenant of thy servant: * thou hast profaned his sanctuary on the earth.

content.latin: 88:41 Destruxísti omnes sepes eius: * posuísti firmaméntum eius formídinem.
content.english: 88:41 Thou hast broken down all his hedges: * thou hast made his strength fear.

content.latin: 88:42 Diripuérunt eum omnes transeúntes viam: * factus est oppróbrium vicínis suis.
content.english: 88:42 All that pass by the way have robbed him: * he is become a reproach to his neighbours.

content.latin: 88:43 Exaltásti déxteram depriméntium eum: * lætificásti omnes inimícos eius.
content.english: 88:43 Thou hast set up the right hand of them that oppress him: * thou hast made all his enemies to rejoice.

content.latin: 88:44 Avertísti adiutórium gládii eius: * et non es auxiliátus ei in bello.
content.english: 88:44 Thou hast turned away the help of his sword; * and hast not assisted him in battle.

content.latin: 88:45 Destruxísti eum ab emundatióne: * et sedem eius in terram collisísti.
content.english: 88:45 Thou hast made his purification to cease: * and thou hast cast his throne down to the ground.

content.latin: 88:46 Minorásti dies témporis eius: * perfudísti eum confusióne.
content.english: 88:46 Thou hast shortened the days of his time: * thou hast covered him with confusion.

content.latin: 88:47 Úsquequo, Dómine, avértis in finem: * exardéscet sicut ignis ira tua?
content.english: 88:47 How long, O Lord, turnest thou away unto the end? * shall thy anger burn like fire?

content.latin: 88:48 Memoráre quæ mea substántia: * numquid enim vane constituísti omnes fílios hóminum?
content.english: 88:48 Remember what my substance is: * for hast thou made all the children of men in vain?

content.latin: 88:49 Quis est homo, qui vivet, et non vidébit mortem: * éruet ánimam suam de manu ínferi?
content.english: 88:49 Who is the man that shall live, and not see death: * that shall deliver his soul from the hand of hell?

content.latin: 88:50 Ubi sunt misericórdiæ tuæ antíquæ, Dómine, * sicut iurásti David in veritáte tua?
content.english: 88:50 Lord, where are thy ancient mercies, * according to what thou didst swear to David in thy truth?

content.latin: 88:51 Memor esto, Dómine, oppróbrii servórum tuórum * quod contínui in sinu meo multárum géntium.
content.english: 88:51 Be mindful, O Lord, of the reproach of thy servants * which I have held in my bosom of many nations:

content.latin: 88:52 Quod exprobravérunt inimíci tui, Dómine, * quod exprobravérunt commutatiónem Christi tui.
content.english: 88:52 Wherewith thy enemies have reproached, O Lord; * wherewith they have reproached the change of thy anointed.

content.latin: 88:53 Benedíctus Dóminus in ætérnum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 88:53 Blessed be the Lord for evermore. * So be it. So be it.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Mercy and truth shall go before thy face, O Lord.

content.latin: Fulgébunt iusti, et tamquam scintíllæ in arundinéto discúrrent. Iudicábunt natiónes, et dominabúntur pópulis: et regnábit Dóminus illórum in perpétuum.
content.english: The just shall shine, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds. They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.
