content.english: ℟.br. The righteous live * for evermore.

content.english: ℟. The righteous live * for evermore.

content.english: ℣. Their reward also is with the Lord.

content.english: ℟. For evermore.

content.english: ℟. They shall be joyful in their beds.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos gemináta lætítia hodiérnæ festivitátis excípiat, quæ de beatórum Ioánnis et Pauli glorificatióne procédit; quos éadem fides et pássio vere fecit esse germános.
content.english: Almighty God, fill us, we beseech thee, with the twofold gladness which doth flow down upon this bright day from the glory of thy blessed servants John and Paul, whom one faith and one suffering made to be brothers indeed.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Ant. Paul and John * said unto Julian: We worship One God, Who hath made heaven and earth.

content.latin: Psalmus 109 [1]
content.english: Psalm 109 [1]

content.latin: 109:1 Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: * Sede a dextris meis:
content.english: 109:1 The Lord said to my Lord: * Sit thou at my right hand:

content.latin: 109:1 Donec ponam inimícos tuos, * scabéllum pedum tuórum.
content.english: 109:1 Until I make thy enemies * thy footstool.

content.latin: 109:2 Virgam virtútis tuæ emíttet Dóminus ex Sion: * domináre in médio inimicórum tuórum.
content.english: 109:2 The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: * rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.

content.latin: 109:3 Tecum princípium in die virtútis tuæ in splendóribus sanctórum: * ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.
content.english: 109:3 With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: * from the womb before the day star I begot thee.

content.latin: 109:4 Iurávit Dóminus, et non pœnitébit eum: * Tu es sacérdos in ætérnum secúndum órdinem Melchísedech.
content.english: 109:4 The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: * Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.

content.latin: 109:5 Dóminus a dextris tuis, * confrégit in die iræ suæ reges.
content.english: 109:5 The Lord at thy right hand * hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.

content.latin: 109:6 Iudicábit in natiónibus, implébit ruínas: * conquassábit cápita in terra multórum.
content.english: 109:6 He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: * he shall crush the heads in the land of many.

content.latin: 109:7 De torrénte in via bibet: * proptérea exaltábit caput.
content.english: 109:7 He shall drink of the torrent in the way: * therefore shall he lift up the head.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. Paul and John said unto Julian: We worship One God, Who hath made heaven and earth.

content.latin: Ant. Paulus et Ioánnes * dixérunt Terentiáno: Si tuus dóminus est Iuliánus, habéto pacem cum illo: nobis álius non est, nisi Dóminus Iesus Christus.
content.english: Ant. Paul and John * said unto Terentian: If thy Lord be Julian, keep thou at peace with him, but as for us, we have no other Lord but the Lord Jesus Christ.

content.latin: Psalmus 110 [2]
content.english: Psalm 110 [2]

content.latin: 110:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * in consílio iustórum, et congregatióne.
content.english: 110:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; * in the council of the just, and in the congregation.

content.latin: 110:2 Magna ópera Dómini: * exquisíta in omnes voluntátes eius.
content.english: 110:2 Great are the works of the Lord: * sought out according to all his wills.

content.latin: 110:3 Conféssio et magnificéntia opus eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:3 His work is praise and magnificence: * and his justice continueth for ever and ever.

content.latin: 110:4 Memóriam fecit mirabílium suórum, miséricors et miserátor Dóminus: * escam dedit timéntibus se.
content.english: 110:4 He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: * he hath given food to them that fear him.

content.latin: 110:5 Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo:
content.english: 110:5 He will be mindful for ever of his covenant: * he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.

content.latin: 110:7 Ut det illis hereditátem géntium: * ópera mánuum eius véritas, et iudícium.
content.english: 110:7 That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: * the works of his hands are truth and judgment.

content.latin: 110:8 Fidélia ómnia mandáta eius: confirmáta in sǽculum sǽculi, * facta in veritáte et æquitáte.
content.english: 110:8 All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, * made in truth and equity.

content.latin: 110:9 Redemptiónem misit pópulo suo: * mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.
content.english: 110:9 He hath sent redemption to his people: * he hath commanded his covenant for ever.

content.latin: 110:9 (fit reverentia) Sanctum, et terríbile nomen eius: * inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
content.english: 110:9 (bow head) Holy and terrible is his name: * the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

content.latin: 110:10 Intelléctus bonus ómnibus faciéntibus eum: * laudátio eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 110:10 A good understanding to all that do it: * his praise continueth for ever and ever.

content.latin: Psalmus 111 [3]
content.english: Psalm 111 [3]

content.latin: 111:1 Beátus vir, qui timet Dóminum: * in mandátis eius volet nimis.
content.english: 111:1 Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord: * he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.

content.latin: 111:2 Potens in terra erit semen eius: * generátio rectórum benedicétur.
content.english: 111:2 His seed shall be mighty upon earth: * the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.

content.latin: 111:3 Glória, et divítiæ in domo eius: * et iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 111:3 Glory and wealth shall be in his house: * and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.

content.latin: 111:4 Exórtum est in ténebris lumen rectis: * miséricors, et miserátor, et iustus.
content.english: 111:4 To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: * he is merciful, and compassionate and just.

content.latin: 111:5 Iucúndus homo qui miserétur et cómmodat, dispónet sermónes suos in iudício: * quia in ætérnum non commovébitur.
content.english: 111:5 Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: he shall order his words with judgment: * because he shall not be moved for ever.

content.latin: 111:7 In memória ætérna erit iustus: * ab auditióne mala non timébit.
content.english: 111:7 The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: * he shall not fear the evil hearing.

content.latin: 111:7 Parátum cor eius speráre in Dómino, confirmátum est cor eius: * non commovébitur donec despíciat inimícos suos.
content.english: 111:7 His heart is ready to hope in the Lord: his heart is strengthened, * he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.

content.latin: 111:9 Dispérsit, dedit paupéribus: iustítia eius manet in sǽculum sǽculi, * cornu eius exaltábitur in glória.
content.english: 111:9 He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: * his horn shall be exalted in glory.

content.latin: 111:10 Peccátor vidébit, et irascétur, déntibus suis fremet et tabéscet: * desidérium peccatórum períbit.
content.english: 111:10 The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: * the desire of the wicked shall perish.

content.english: Ant. O ye holy Spirits and Souls of the righteous, bless ye the Lord. Alleluia.

content.latin: Psalmus 112 [4]
content.english: Psalm 112 [4]

content.latin: 112:1 Laudáte, púeri, Dóminum: * laudáte nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:1 Praise the Lord, ye children: * praise ye the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 112:2 (fit reverentia) Sit nomen Dómini benedíctum, * ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum.
content.english: 112:2 (bow head) Blessed be the name of the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

content.latin: 112:3 A solis ortu usque ad occásum, * laudábile nomen Dómini.
content.english: 112:3 From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, * the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.

content.latin: 112:4 Excélsus super omnes gentes Dóminus, * et super cælos glória eius.
content.english: 112:4 The Lord is high above all nations; * and his glory above the heavens.

content.latin: 112:5 Quis sicut Dóminus, Deus noster, qui in altis hábitat, * et humília réspicit in cælo et in terra?
content.english: 112:5 Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high: * and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?

content.latin: 112:7 Súscitans a terra ínopem, * et de stércore érigens páuperem:
content.english: 112:7 Raising up the needy from the earth, * and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:

content.latin: 112:8 Ut cóllocet eum cum princípibus, * cum princípibus pópuli sui.
content.english: 112:8 That he may place him with princes, * with the princes of his people.

content.latin: 112:9 Qui habitáre facit stérilem in domo, * matrem filiórum lætántem.
content.english: 112:9 Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, * the joyful mother of children.

content.latin: Psalmus 116 [5]
content.english: Psalm 116 [5]

content.latin: 116:1 Laudáte Dóminum, omnes gentes: * laudáte eum, omnes pópuli:
content.english: 116:1 Praise the Lord, all ye nations: * praise him, all ye people.

content.latin: 116:2 Quóniam confirmáta est super nos misericórdia eius: * et véritas Dómini manet in ætérnum.
content.english: 116:2 For his mercy is confirmed upon us: * and the truth of the Lord remaineth for ever.

content.latin: Iustórum ánimæ in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos torméntum mortis. Visi sunt óculis insipiéntium mori: illi autem sunt in pace.
content.english: But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them. In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die, but they are in peace.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

content.latin: Sanctórum méritis ínclita gáudia
content.english: Sing, O sons of the Church sounding the martyrs' praise!

content.latin: Pangámus, sócii, géstaque fórtia:
content.english: God's true soldiers applaud, who, in their weary days,

content.latin: Gliscens fert ánimus prómere cántibus
content.english: Won bright trophies of good, glad be the voice ye raise,

content.latin: Victórum genus óptimum.
content.english: While these heroes of Christ ye sing!

content.latin: Hi sunt, quos fátue mundus abhórruit;
content.english: They, while yet in the world were by the world abhorred;

content.latin: Hunc fructu vácuum, flóribus áridum
content.english: Felt how fading the joys, fleeting the wealth it stored;

content.latin: Contempsére tui nóminis ásseclæ
content.english: Spurned all pleasure for thee, and at thy call, O Lord,

content.latin: Iesu, Rex bone cǽlitum.
content.english: Came forth strong in thy name, as King.

content.latin: Hi pro te fúrias, atque minas truces
content.english: Lord, how bravely they bore fury and pain for thee!

content.latin: Calcárunt hóminum, sǽvaque vérbera:
content.english: Scourge, rod, sword, and the rack strongly endured; but free

content.latin: His cessit lácerans fórtiter úngula,
content.english: Sang out, bold in thy love, longing on high to be;

content.latin: Nec carpsit penetrália.
content.english: Earth's might never their souls could bend.

content.latin: Cædúntur gládiis more bidéntium:
content.english: While they, shedding their blood, victims for Jesus fell,

content.latin: Non murmur résonat, non quærimónia;
content.english: No sound out of their lips came of their throes to tell;

content.latin: Sed corde impávido mens bene cónscia
content.english: Bowed low, patient and meek, loving the Lord so well,

content.latin: Consérvat patiéntiam.
content.english: Turned they still to the Christ, their friend.

content.latin: Quæ vox, quæ póterit lingua retéxere,
content.english: What joys, bright with the blood shed for thy love they share,

content.latin: Quæ tu Martýribus múnera prǽparas?
content.english: Those brave martyrs of thine crowned with thy laurels rare;

content.latin: Rubri nam flúido sánguine fúlgidis
content.english: Man's tongue never can tell, never can half declare,

content.latin: Cingunt témpora láureis.
content.english: How pure now is their bliss above!

content.latin: Te, summa o Déitas, únaque póscimus;
content.english: Yet we, Father on high, God of eternal might,

content.latin: Ut culpas ábigas, nóxia súbtrahas,
content.english: Lift weak voices in prayer asking for peace and light;

content.latin: Des pacem fámulis; ut tibi glóriam,
content.english: Cleanse thou out of our hearts every stain and blight,

content.latin: Annórum in sériem, canant.
content.english: So our songs may be songs of love.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Ioánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, et ómnibus Sanctis, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: percutit sibi pectus mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ídeo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Ioánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, et omnes Sanctos, oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
content.english: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

content.latin: Misereátur nostri omnípotens Deus, et dimíssis peccátis nostris, perdúcat nos ad vitam ætérnam. Amen.
content.english: May almighty God have mercy on us, forgive us our sins, and bring us to everlasting life. Amen.

content.latin: 76:2 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * voce mea ad Deum, et inténdit mihi.
content.english: 76:2 I cried to the Lord with my voice; * to God with my voice, and he gave ear to me.

content.latin: 76:3 In die tribulatiónis meæ Deum exquisívi, mánibus meis nocte contra eum: * et non sum decéptus.
content.english: 76:3 In the day of my trouble I sought God, with my hands lifted up to him in the night, * and I was not deceived.

content.latin: 76:4 Rénuit consolári ánima mea, * memor fui Dei, et delectátus sum, et exercitátus sum: et defécit spíritus meus.
content.english: 76:4 My soul refused to be comforted: * I remembered God, and was delighted, and was exercised, and my spirit swooned away.

content.latin: 76:5 Anticipavérunt vigílias óculi mei: * turbátus sum, et non sum locútus.
content.english: 76:5 My eyes prevented the watches: * I was troubled, and I spoke not.

content.latin: 76:6 Cogitávi dies antíquos: * et annos ætérnos in mente hábui.
content.english: 76:6 I thought upon the days of old: * and I had in my mind the eternal years.

content.latin: 76:7 Et meditátus sum nocte cum corde meo, * et exercitábar, et scopébam spíritum meum.
content.english: 76:7 And I meditated in the night with my own heart: * and I was exercised and I swept my spirit.

content.latin: 76:8 Numquid in ætérnum proíciet Deus: * aut non appónet ut complacítior sit adhuc?
content.english: 76:8 Will God then cast off for ever? * or will he never be more favourable again?

content.latin: 76:9 Aut in finem misericórdiam suam abscíndet, * a generatióne in generatiónem?
content.english: 76:9 Or will he cut off his mercy for ever, * from generation to generation?

content.latin: 76:10 Aut obliviscétur miseréri Deus? * aut continébit in ira sua misericórdias suas?
content.english: 76:10 Or will God forget to shew mercy? * or will he in his anger shut up his mercies?

content.latin: 76:11 Et dixi: Nunc cœpi: * hæc mutátio déxteræ Excélsi.
content.english: 76:11 And I said, Now have I begun: * this is the change of the right hand of the most High.

content.latin: 76:12 Memor fui óperum Dómini: * quia memor ero ab inítio mirabílium tuórum.
content.english: 76:12 I remembered the works of the Lord: * for I will be mindful of thy wonders from the beginning.

content.latin: 76:13 Et meditábor in ómnibus opéribus tuis: * et in adinventiónibus tuis exercébor.
content.english: 76:13 And I will meditate on all thy works: * and will be employed in thy inventions.

content.latin: 76:15 Notam fecísti in pópulis virtútem tuam: * redemísti in brácchio tuo pópulum tuum, fílios Iacob et Ioseph.
content.english: 76:15 Thou hast made thy power known among the nations: * with thy arm thou hast redeemed thy people, the children of Jacob and of Joseph.

content.latin: 76:17 Vidérunt te aquæ, Deus, vidérunt te aquæ: * et timuérunt, et turbátæ sunt abýssi.

content.latin: 76:18 Multitúdo sónitus aquárum: * vocem dedérunt nubes.

content.latin: 76:18 Étenim sagíttæ tuæ tránseunt: * vox tonítrui tui in rota.
content.english: 76:18 For thy arrows pass: * the voice of thy thunder in a wheel.

content.latin: 76:19 Illuxérunt coruscatiónes tuæ orbi terræ: * commóta est, et contrémuit terra.
content.english: 76:19 Thy lightnings enlightened the world: * the earth shook and trembled.

content.latin: 76:20 In mari via tua, et sémitæ tuæ in aquis multis: * et vestígia tua non cognoscéntur.
content.english: 76:20 Thy way is in the sea, and thy paths in many waters: * and thy footsteps shall not be known.

content.latin: 85:1 Inclína, Dómine, aurem tuam, et exáudi me: * quóniam inops, et pauper sum ego.
content.english: 85:1 Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear me: * for I am needy and poor.

content.latin: 85:2 Custódi ánimam meam, quóniam sanctus sum: * salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperántem in te.
content.english: 85:2 Preserve my soul, for I am holy: * save thy servant, O my God, that trusteth in thee.

content.latin: 85:3 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam ad te clamávi tota die: * lætífica ánimam servi tui, quóniam ad te, Dómine, ánimam meam levávi.
content.english: 85:3 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I have cried to thee all the day. * Give joy to the soul of thy servant, for to thee, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

content.latin: 85:5 Quóniam tu, Dómine, suávis, et mitis: * et multæ misericórdiæ ómnibus invocántibus te.
content.english: 85:5 For thou, O Lord, art sweet and mild: * and plenteous in mercy to all that call upon thee.

content.latin: 85:6 Áuribus pércipe, Dómine, oratiónem meam: * et inténde voci deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 85:6 Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer: * and attend to the voice of my petition.

content.latin: 85:7 In die tribulatiónis meæ clamávi ad te: * quia exaudísti me.
content.english: 85:7 I have called upon thee in the day of my trouble: * because thou hast heard me.

content.latin: 85:8 Non est símilis tui in diis, Dómine: * et non est secúndum ópera tua.
content.english: 85:8 There is none among the gods like unto thee, O Lord: * and there is none according to thy works.

content.latin: 85:9 Omnes gentes quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine: * et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
content.english: 85:9 All the nations thou hast made shall come and adore before thee, O Lord: * and they shall glorify thy name.

content.latin: 85:10 Quóniam magnus es tu, et fáciens mirabília: * tu es Deus solus.
content.english: 85:10 For thou art great and dost wonderful things: * thou art God alone.

content.latin: 85:11 Deduc me, Dómine, in via tua, et ingrédiar in veritáte tua: * lætétur cor meum ut tímeat nomen tuum.
content.english: 85:11 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way, and I will walk in thy truth: * let my heart rejoice that it may fear thy name.

content.latin: 85:12 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Deus meus, in toto corde meo, * et glorificábo nomen tuum in ætérnum:
content.english: 85:12 I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, * and I will glorify thy name for ever:

content.latin: 85:13 Quia misericórdia tua magna est super me: * et eruísti ánimam meam ex inférno inferióri.
content.english: 85:13 For thy mercy is great towards me: * and thou hast delivered my soul out of the lower hell.

content.latin: 85:14 Deus, iníqui insurrexérunt super me, et synagóga poténtium quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt te in conspéctu suo.
content.english: 85:14 O God, the wicked are risen up against me, and the assembly of the mighty have sought my soul: * and they have not set thee before their eyes.

content.latin: 85:15 Et tu, Dómine, Deus miserátor et miséricors, * pátiens, et multæ misericórdiæ, et verax,
content.english: 85:15 And thou, O Lord, art a God of compassion, and merciful, * patient, and of much mercy, and true.

content.latin: 85:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei, * da impérium tuum púero tuo: et salvum fac fílium ancíllæ tuæ.
content.english: 85:16 O look upon me, and have mercy on me: * give thy command to thy servant, and save the son of thy handmaid.

content.latin: 85:17 Fac mecum signum in bonum, ut vídeant qui odérunt me, et confundántur: * quóniam tu, Dómine, adiuvísti me, et consolátus es me.
content.english: 85:17 Shew me a token for good: that they who hate me may see, and be confounded, * because thou, O Lord, hast helped me and hast comforted me.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salva nos, Dómine, vigilántes, custódi nos dormiéntes; ut vigilémus cum Christo, et requiescámus in pace.
content.english: Ant. Protect us, Lord, while we are awake and safeguard us while we sleep; that we may keep watch with Christ, and rest in peace.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Vísita, quǽsumus, Dómine, habitatiónem istam, et omnes insídias inimíci ab ea longe repélle: Ángeli tui sancti hábitent in ea, qui nos in pace custódiant; et benedíctio tua sit super nos semper.
content.english: Visit, we beseech thee, O Lord, this dwelling, and drive far from it the snares of the enemy; let thy holy angels dwell herein to preserve us in peace, and let thy blessing be always upon us.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedícat et custódiat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus, ✠ Pater, et Fílius, et Spíritus Sanctus.
content.english: Benediction. The almighty and merciful Lord, ✠ the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless us and keep us.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ;
content.english: Hail holy Queen, Mother of Mercy,

content.latin: vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve.
content.english: our life, our sweetness, and our hope.

content.latin: Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ.
content.english: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

content.latin: Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes
content.english: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping

content.latin: In hac lacrimárum valle.
content.english: In this valley of tears.

content.latin: Eia ergo, advocáta nostra,
content.english: Turn then, most gracious Advocate,

content.latin: illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte.
content.english: thine eyes of mercy toward us.

content.latin: Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,
content.english: And after this our exile show unto us

content.latin: nobis post hoc exsílium osténde.
content.english: the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

content.latin: O clemens, o pia, o dulcis Virgo María.
content.english: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

content.latin: ℣. Ora pro nobis, sancta Dei Génetrix.
content.english: ℣. Pray for us, O Holy Mother of God.

content.latin: ℟. Ut digni efficiámur promissiónibus Christi.
content.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui gloriósæ Vírginis Matris Maríæ corpus et ánimam, ut dignum Fílii tui habitáculum éffici mererétur, Spíritu Sancto cooperánte, præparásti: da, ut, cuius commemoratióne lætámur, eius pia intercessióne, ab instántibus malis et a morte perpétua liberémur. Per eúndem Christum Dóminum nostrum. Amen.
content.english: O almighty, everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, didst prepare the body and soul of Mary, glorious Virgin and Mother, to become a worthy dwelling for Thy Son; grant that we who rejoice in her commemoration may, by her gracious intercession, be delivered from present evils and from everlasting death. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Divínum auxílium ✠ máneat semper nobíscum.
content.english: ℣. May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.
